title: Struggling through high school and Howard; the Howard Theatre audition
summary: Juggling gigs and mathematics he barely finished high school and college sophomore year at Howard; at sixteen he auditioned at the Howard Theatre for Sylvester Lewis and was sent away for being underage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So, all right, I stayed with them a long time till I got -- but what was happening to me, I was having -- my last year of high school, I was having a big problem, see, trying to make those gigs and try to study, and study those books, the

mathematical was about eating me up, but those people they was going to the dances and so on, I passed, but when I got to the sophomore year in college, it was rough, rough, rough and I barely made it, I just barely made it, but then I'm getting more worldly with the instrument.

Howard University, because see at that time Duke had left there. Claude Hopkins' family, I think they was -- his mother or something was a professor or somebody dean or something, see, Claude Hopkins was a very high class individual. He's a dogmatic man, but in his way, he's all right. He's beautiful. That's the real Washingtonian way and by the way, Sonny Greer will tell you about those Washingtonian, and then I went to the theatre, the Howard Theatre one time and I looked at the show, it was called Shake Your Feet Revue, and I saw the trumpet player. I said well, I should be down there and leave here. See, I want to leave now. So I went down there and met a fellow named Sylvester Lewis, and he said, yes, we need a second trumpet, so I got out there and I read the music pretty good and there was another friend of mine named Herbie Cowans, boy from Texas. He said, by the way, how old are you. I was about 16 then, and he said you get out of here, man, they'd put him in jail.
